verdict.rationale: Keycloak ships strong headless-automation primitives: it can be started fully via Docker/container images with env-var bootstrap (keycloak-docs-2, keycloak-docs-45), has a scriptable Admin CLI (kcadm.sh) and REST Admin API for realm/user/client management (kc-supp-kcadm, keycloak-docs-6), supports realm import/export as JSON for declarative setup (keycloak-docs-10, keycloak-docs-76), and exposes health endpoints for readiness checks useful in CI pipelines (keycloak-docs-17). However, community reports describe real friction running it headlessly in automated/IaC pipelines: it 'doesn't play well with infrastructure-as-code ideas' (keycloak-comm-3), the Admin API is 'inconsistent' making idempotent automation hard (keycloak-comm-13), and configuration lives in the database rather than files, blocking config-as-code testing before production (keycloak-comm-19). Missing for 10: first-party CI/automation guide or GitHub Actions example, evidence of clean idempotent scripted provisioning, and resolution of the documented IaC friction.
